ShouldDisappearFromDoom.maps_to: no sim counterpart (presentation; the sim has no Doom)
ShouldDisappearFromDoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 4 named this the one presentation-looking hook not to reflex-waive, and TWO batches answered it differently, which is exactly the gap-detector governing rule 3 describes. RECONCILED 2026-07-27 by the stream lead reading DoomPower.cs end to end; NEITHER original answer was right. (a) There IS exactly one reader -- `grep -rn ShouldDisappearFromDoom --include=*.cs src/` returns 11 lines: the MonsterModel virtual, nine monster overrides, and ONE consumer, DoomPower.cs:90. So the batch-8 claim that every site is a declaration is false. (b) But that reader does NOT gate removal, so the batch-5 claim that the creature 'is NOT removed when DoomPower's kill sweep fires' is false too. DoomPower.cs:90 sits inside `private static async Task PlayVfx`, which early-returns when the creature has no visual node (DoomPower.cs:82-86). Its result feeds exactly two things: StartDoomAnim(nCreature, flag) and a Cmd.Wait(0.25f)/Cmd.Wait(1.5f) timing branch (DoomPower.cs:101-111). StartDoomAnim's shouldDie arm (DoomPower.cs:117-134) is Monster?.OnDieToDoom(), an AnimDisableUi tween, QueueFreeSafely, a Spine 'Hit' trigger, NCombatRoom.RemoveCreatureNode (the NODE, i.e. the view) and the NDoomVfx variant. OnDieToDoom is documented at MonsterModel.cs:485-491 as 'Primarily used set up the creature visuals for the Doom vfx', its base body is empty, and its single override in the game (TorchHeadAmalgam.cs:67-79) hides three light nodes. (c) The death itself is unconditional and OUTSIDE PlayVfx: DoomPower.DoomKill (DoomPower.cs:40-53) is `await PlayVfx(creature); await CreatureCmd.Kill(creature);`. So the property decides whether the sprite vanishes with the doom animation, never whether the creature dies or leaves Enemies -- presentation, `waiver`, matching monster_state_machine N2 and the KinPriest N6 precedent. Same verdict at all nine C# overriders (CeremonialBeast, Crusher, DecimillipedeSegment, EyeWithTeeth, Parafright, Rocket, TestSubject, Vantom, WaterfallGiant) per rule 3. Per rule 7: DoomPower.cs, MonsterModel.cs and TorchHeadAmalgam.cs are cited with line numbers and are NOT hashed by this record.

AfterAddedToRoom.maps_to: Rocket.__init__ -> PowerCmd.apply(SurroundedPower, 1) on the PLAYER, then BackAttackRightPower 1 and CrabRagePower 1 on itself (kaiser_crab.py:108-116)
AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: ESCALATED rather than inherited from SHARED-FINDINGS section 2, because Rocket is the single ported monster that applies a power to the PLAYER from its constructor and section 2's clause (a) is argued for self-applied powers. Rocket.cs:93-95 applies SurroundedPower 1m to base.CombatState.GetOpponentsOf(base.Creature) - in Ironclad scope, the one player - with applier = the Rocket, then BackAttackRightPower 1m and CrabRagePower 1m to itself; kaiser_crab.py:112-116 does the same three in the same order. Executed with `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b05.py rocket-ctor`, which instruments the moment Rocket.__init__ runs: hooks.combat is NOT None and combat.player already exists (combat.py assigns both before create_monsters), so the `if combat is not None` guard at kaiser_crab.py:113 is not silently skipping the power - the probe confirms the player ends up with powers=['surrounded'], amount 1, applier=Rocket, facing 'right'. What does NOT exist yet is combat.enemies (`combat has .enemies = False`), and SurroundedPower's only read of it is in on_death (powers.py:2585-2593), never at apply time - so the missing list is unobservable here. Nor do relics or belt potions exist yet (`combat has .relics = False`, `belt potions registered = False`; listener set at that instant is CombatHistory, the deck's StrikeCard/DefendCard instances and Crusher's own two powers). That matters more than for a self-applied power because the TARGET is the player: the two ported modify_power_amount implementers were read individually - relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38 gates on power_cls is StrengthPower (Surrounded is not), and relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53 returns early on both `self._in_flight is None` (no card is resolving during combat construction) and `target is self.player` - so neither can fire, and `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b05.py listeners` shows those two are the ONLY implementers outside hooks.py. Finally, SurroundedPower is PowerType.DEBUFF (powers.py:2537), so PowerCmd.apply's Artifact interception (cmds.py:299-306) is on the path; the probe prints `player.powers artifact present at ctor time? False`, and the game cannot differ because every relic that could grant Artifact does so no earlier than Hook.BeforeCombatStart (CombatManager.cs:403), which runs AFTER AfterCreatureAdded (:394-398). Concrete trigger that would make this a gap: any relic or potion listening on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied without gating on the player as applier, or a player-side Artifact source that attaches before combat construction. Rule 7: leans on sts2_rl/powers.py, sts2_rl/cmds.py, sts2_rl/combat.py, sts2_rl/relics/ruined_helmet.py, sts2_rl/relics/unsettling_lamp.py and src/Core/Combat/CombatManager.cs, none of which this record hashes.

Read to the end, independently of Crusher's (rule 29): guard `creature != base.Creature || delta >= 0m`, then the whole body is Background.PlayHurtAnim(NKaiserCrabBossBackground.ArmSide.Right) (Rocket.cs:99-107). ArmSide.Right is the only difference from Crusher's; both are pure animation. Presentation, SHARED-FINDINGS section 4.

BeforeDeath.rationale: Read to the end and compared with Crusher's line by line rather than copied (rule 29). Rocket.cs:109-127: guard on creature identity, NAudioManager.PlayOneShot(DeathSfx), Background.PlayArmDeathAnim(ArmSide.Right), then the IsOverOrEnding branch - body death animation plus music parameter 5f, ELSE music parameter 1f. Crusher's else arm sets 2f (Crusher.cs:147). So the two siblings DO differ, and the difference is exactly one FMOD parameter value (which arm died first drives the boss music tier) plus the arm side. Nothing mechanical on either side. Presentation.

BeforeRemovedFromRoom.rationale: Presentation only (SHARED-FINDINGS section 4): no mechanical reader. Rocket.cs:129-132 is a single SfxCmd.StopLoop of the charge-up loop started by ChargeUpMove; the sim models no looping sfx.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Five-node fixed cycle, no branch state and no RNG. C# (Rocket.cs:69-88): TARGETING_RETICLE -> PRECISION_BEAM -> CHARGE_UP -> LASER -> RECHARGE -> TARGETING_RETICLE, registered in that order, initialState = TARGETING_RETICLE. The sim wires the identical ring, registration order and initial state. RECHARGE is a genuinely empty move on both sides (Rocket.cs:170-174 is sfx and a background animation only; kaiser_crab.py:155-156 is `pass`), carrying SleepIntent -> Intent(MoveType.SLEEP).

guards.what: GetOpponentsOf resolves to the players, not to the other arm
guards.rationale: CombatState.cs:389-392 GetOpponentsOf returns GetCreaturesOnSide(creature.Side.GetOppositeSide()) - for an enemy that is the player side, so Surrounded lands on the player and never on Crusher. The sim targets combat.player directly. CombatState.cs is in extra_sources.

guards.what: creation order of the two arms
guards.rationale: KAISER_CRAB_BOSS is monster_classes=[Crusher, Rocket] (kaiser_crab.py:159-162), so Crusher's BackAttackLeftPower is already on the board when Rocket's Surrounded is applied - executed by the rocket-ctor probe, whose listener snapshot contains BackAttackLeftPower and CrabRagePower. That ordering is what makes SurroundedPower's initial facing meaningful, and the probe prints facing='right' (the Rocket side) for a fresh combat.
